# add homebrew to path

Put Apple-Silicon Homebrew on `PATH`. The installer's closing advice on a new M1 Mac:

```
- Run these two commands in your terminal to add Homebrew to your PATH:
    echo 'eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"' >> /Users/.../.zprofile
    eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
```

`/opt/homebrew/bin` is not in the system default `PATH` (unlike `/usr/local/bin` on Intel), so without this step nothing installed by the Brewfile is found in new shells, and the installer's own next step failed ([[DOT-200]]).

<!-- 2026-09-16T05:49Z https://github.com/kamilsk/dotfiles/issues/205#issuecomment-5711690106
Code vs intent: Homebrew's prefix is hard-coded to `/opt/homebrew` in `env.bash`; Intel (`/usr/local`) and Linuxbrew only get `PATH` via the installer's one-off `eval "$(brew shellenv)"`. The `path has` helper in the same file clobbers `PATH` under zsh (see the note on #255).
